form_title: 2010 FINANCIAL CAMPAIGN REPORT FOR COUNTY CANDIDATES (Utah County Code 2-5 & Utah State Code 17-16-6.5)

reports.report_type_printed: Seven days preceding the Primary Election
reports.notes: Handwritten cursive, crisp. LINE 3 is written '$0.0' with a horizontal stroke drawn through it - it reads as the filer's zero with a cancel/emphasis line, but no replacement figure is written above or beside it, so the surviving value is transcribed as '0.0' at LOW confidence; nothing was inferred and no arithmetic was used. LINE 7 is written inside hand-drawn parentheses/angle brackets: '($3.46)' - the accountant's convention for a negative amount. It is transcribed VERBATIM with the parentheses ('(3.46)') rather than converted to '-3.46', so the build layer decides how to read the sign. Lines 1 and 4/5 mix forms: line 1 is bare '500' in both columns, line 4 is '500' with a raised '00', line 5 is '500.00' written out - all kept as printed. AMENDMENT: the 'No' box carries a check mark. office_index said 'County Treasurer'; the page's Office Seeking field says just 'Treasurer' (naming-convention difference, not a conflict). candidate_index was blank; the page names Robert Kirk. The clerk's FILED stamp (upside-down on the scan) reads '10 JUN 11 PM 4:49'.

contributions.note: THE DATE IS KEPT VERBATIM AS '2/09' AND IS FLAGGED, NOT REPAIRED. It carries only two components, so it is either February 2009 — sixteen months before this report and before the cycle it belongs to — or a day-and-month with the year omitted; the page does not say which, and neither a day nor a year is ever filled in from the report date. Both readings are anomalous and both are honest; the build's date normalizer will blank it with needs_review, which is the correct outcome. THE AMOUNT IS WRITTEN '$500' WITH NO CENTS AT ALL and is recorded as the plain decimal 500.00. THE MAILING-ADDRESS CELL IS LEFT ENTIRELY EMPTY BY THE FILER — it is not redacted (this 2010 file carries no redaction bars and the cover's own address block is fully visible) — so donor_city and donor_state are honestly blank. The donor is an organisation, not a person.

contributions.detail: The single Schedule A row sums to 500.00 = the schedule's printed page subtotal ($500) = its printed Total Contributions Received ($500) = the cover's PROMOTED per-period cell Column A line 1 ($500), confirmed by a 900 dpi crop of pct:74,85,22,9@p3 which rendered both bottom-of-page cells as '$500'. Column B 'Year-to-Date Total' also prints $500 and is NOT summed as an increment; it equals Column A here only because this is the FIRST report of the 2010 cycle, so the period IS the year to date — this is NOT a cumulative-scoped schedule and the verdict is `exact`, not `cumulative-exact`. The p2 balance ladder closes: line 3 (0) + line 4 (500.00) = line 5 (500.00); 500.00 - line 6 (503.46) = line 7, which the filer wrote as a negative in ANGLE BRACKETS.

expenditures.anchor: Column A 'Total this Period' line 2 TOTAL EXPENDITURES MADE ($503.46) on the p2 Summary Page, equal to Schedule B's own printed 'Subtotal for this page' (503.46) and its printed 'Total Expenditures Received' (503.46), and echoed at summary line 6 ($503.46)
expenditures.detail: The 3 written Schedule B entries sum to 473.46 + 25.00 + 5.00 = 503.46 EXACTLY = the printed page subtotal = the printed total = the cover's promoted per-period Column A (900 dpi crop of pct:74,85.5,22,9@p4 rendered both bottom cells as '$503.46'). THE CLOSURE IS ALSO WHAT FIXES ROW 1's AMOUNT: at 2000 dpi that cell renders as '473' and '46' with NO decimal separator written between them, and the value 473.46 is determined uniquely by the arithmetic (503.46 - 25.00 - 5.00 = 473.46) rather than by the glyph — the GOTCHAS ruling that arithmetic closure outranks glyph reading, applied where the closure IS unique. A FOURTH PRINTED ROW WAS VOIDED BY THE FILER AND IS NOT AN ENTRY: printed row 3 carries a struck-through date and nothing else (see the notes), so it contributes nothing to the sum and the third real entry sits on printed row 4. Column B YTD expenditures also print 503.46 and are never summed as an increment; they equal Column A because this is the cycle's first report.

itemized.in_kind_convention: monetary-only closed BOTH sides exactly (500.00 and 503.46). Both conventions were tested per the brief and coincide here: neither schedule prints an in-kind column, the cover prints no in-kind line, and no row bears an in-kind marking, so monetary-only and monetary-plus-in-kind give identical sums.

itemized.notes: PAGE-FACE CANDIDATE: 'Robert Kirk' — index.csv names NO candidate for this row (the 2008-2018 county_static listing grouped filings by office), so the page face governs and is offered to the coordinator for promotion into that EMPTY channel cell. Office Seeking written simply 'Treasurer' (the index/channel office is 'County Treasurer' — the same office, not a disagreement); party 'Republican'; residence city Lehi, Utah (street line printed unredacted on the cover and deliberately not carried). legacy_colAB variant on the '2010 FINANCIAL CAMPAIGN REPORT ... (Utah County Code 2-5)' blank, 4 pages, each classified from its OWN printed header: p1 COVER, p2 SUMMARY PAGE, p3 SCHEDULE A, p4 SCHEDULE B. Report type 'Seven days preceding the Primary Election', marked X; amendment answered 'No'; signed 6-11-10. ~ A VOIDED PRINTED ROW — THE MOST IMPORTANT PROPERTY OF THIS FILING. Schedule B's printed row 3 carries a date, '5/9/10', with a single ink stroke drawn straight through it, and NOTHING in the payee, address or amount columns. The filer began an entry, struck the date and abandoned the line. It is NOT an entry (no payee, no amount, and it contributes nothing to a subtotal that closes exactly without it), but it DOES consume a printed row, so the filing's third real expenditure sits on printed line 4. This is the base brief's continuation/consumed-row trap in a new form — a struck row rather than a wrapped address — and NO ARITHMETIC GATE COULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, because the voided line carries no figure; only the per-band crops did. Both the amount-column crop (empty) and the date-column crop (the struck date) are recorded in escalation_note. ~ THE FILER CORRECTED THE COUNTY'S OWN SCHEDULE B HEADER, striking the word 'Contributor' out of the printed 'Name of Contributor' and writing 'payee' beside it. That is the THIRD filer in this chunk to fix that mislabel by hand (Gary Ratcliffe wrote 'Recipient' over it on both his 2010 schedules), which makes it a recurring source property of the 2010 blank rather than one filer's quirk. ~ THE CLERK'S FILED STAMP IS PRINTED UPSIDE-DOWN in the 'For Office Use Only' box — 'FILED UTAH COUNTY / 10 JUN 11 PM 4:49 / CLERK / AUDITOR' reads inverted. This is the SECOND upside-down clerk stamp in this chunk (the Peterson filing carries one at the page foot), so the inverted stamp is a routine 2010 clerk-desk artifact, not a one-off. Receipt date 11 June 2010 matches the filer's own signature date exactly. ~ FOLIATION: the page header box is filled on Schedule B ('Kirk', '6-11-10') and on the Summary Page, but is LEFT ENTIRELY BLANK on Schedule A, and the Page/of cells are blank on every sheet — a fourth foliation behaviour in this chunk and another demonstration that a page ordinal locates nothing. ~ TWO COVER-FIGURE CONVENTIONS WORTH RECORDING (neither affects a row): line 3 'Balance at Beginning' is written '$0.0' with a horizontal stroke drawn through it — the filer's own nil mark, read 0 under the ZERO-GLYPH RULING and confirmed by the ladder — and line 7 'Balance at Close' is written in ANGLE BRACKETS as ⟨$3.46⟩, i.e. a NEGATIVE 3.46 in the accountant's-parentheses convention rendered with angle brackets instead of round ones. The ladder closes on it: 0 + 500.00 - 503.46 = -3.46. ~ BOTH SIDES CLOSE EXACTLY on the promoted per-period Column A.
